proof.criterion: Review finding 4 (important): part ids are matched to options and to the answer by what identifies the part, so an index behind its row and an older event payload carry no wrong ids.
proof.surface: The same running Dispatch, over HTTP, with the ask row moved under the index by a direct SQL update (what a stale index or an older build leaves).
proof.command: update asks set options = … / jsonb_set(answer,'{text}',…) directly in PostgreSQL, then GET /api/v1/asks/<id>; and GET /api/v1/issues/<key>/events after an edit that replaced both options
proof.observed: An option no stored part stands for carries id null (Gamma null, Beta keeps b3). Two options swapped under the index keep their own ids — Beta b3, Alpha b2 — so an id follows the text and not the position. A row that grows gives the new option none; one that shrinks keeps the survivor's. An answer rewritten under the index carries none. On the events route the ask.opened payload of an ask whose two options were later replaced carries id null for both, while ask.edited carries the current b2 and b3.
proof.negativeControl: The swap is the control for position matching: a matcher that fell back to position would answer Beta b2 and Alpha b3, the finding's defect, and it answers Beta b3 and Alpha b2.

proof.criterion: Review finding 5 (important): the part's heading does not depend on a request that can fail the whole read.
proof.surface: The real dispatch CLI against the same server.
proof.command: dispatch read --ref 'dispatch://KEY/ask/<id>#b-b1' and '#b-b2' on a clean ask, and the same on an ask whose index is behind its row
proof.observed: A clean ask prints "Question b1 of ask <id> (changed in revision 1):" and "Option b2 of ask <id> (changed in revision 1):". Where the index is behind the row the heading degrades to "Part b1 of ask <id>", the conservative answer, since the read cannot then prove which part the question is. The ask read is now advisory — client.getAsk(...).catch(() => undefined) at dispatch-execute.ts:4703 — so a failure of it leaves the part under "Part" and the rest of the read unchanged.
proof.negativeControl: The stale-index ask is the control: it is the state in which the client may not claim "Question", and it does not.
